newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark gains, hold above 1.68 seen key.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark gains, hold above 1.68 seen key.

text.p: The dollar pushed back above the 1.69 mark level by mid-morning, cheering chartists who said the rate's ability to hold above the key 1.68 threshold was pivotal.

"The 1.6800 area in dollar/mark is key support," said Scott Siller, senior technical analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch. "It's the neckline of a head and shoulders top pattern and that area could be a trigger for a medium term correction to the 1.6625 area."
Siller said his revised bull channel support line in dollar/mark came in at 1.6625.
The dollar's failure to get to channel resistance near the 1.71 area over the past several days led to a flattening of Siller's bull channel for the rate, he said.
At 1045 EST/1545 GMT, dollar/mark was trading at 1.6900/05 and dollar/yen had moved back above the 123 level.

Pete Grant, senior foreign exchange analyst at MMS International, said a break of Wednesday's low around 1.68 would extend dollar/mark losses to the mid-1.6700s, but viewed any such price action as a buying opportunity.
"We're oversold on an intraday basis and I think the overall dollar tone remains positive," said Grant.
In dollar/yen, technicians cited firm trendline support dating back to early January at 122.50, but said the 124.70/80 barrier appeared daunting.

"In order to perpetuate this uptrend we really have to break above that fairly quickly," said Grant, noting that more consolidation rather than any outright correction was the most likely near-term scenario.
He said that barring a near-term break below the 121 level, his upside objective in dollar/yen remained at 126.21, the high from January 13 of 1993.
